title: FROM POLICY TO PLACE
blurb: In 2013, South Australia's Small Venue Licence changed the rules.. — allowing small bars of limited capacity and trading hours and without the need for lengthily license applications and court costs. — and transformed Adelaide's laneways. This panels discussion explores how that policy shift unleashed a wave of design creativity, turning tight budgets and small footprints into intimate, distinctive venues that reshaped the city's cultural identity.
contributors: Designer a bar owner a government praetive; a comumunity advocate

title: OBJECT TO MATERIAL
blurb: Object to Material showcases a series of furniture & homeware each made of common objects like soda cans, milk bottles, etc. The need for such furniture arises when people, like students, rent an unfurnished house with limited funds. Characteristics such as playfulness, peculiar visual language is highlighted in each piece.
contributors: Achintya Chaudhary; Laura Sandil; (Venue Collaboration with Marchelle Matthew)

title: MOVEMENT ACROSS SCALES
blurb: Woods Bagot welcomes visitors to an open studio and curated exhibition exploring how design shapes movement and connection from city streets to national transport networks. Centred on the human experience, it reveals how architecture and infrastructure influence journeys across increasingly complex systems.

title: DESIGN FOR CARE
blurb: The Design for Care exhibition presents design and co-design projects that reimagine how healthcare systems, services, and products are created. Through collaborative work between Adelaide University researchers, designers, healthcare professionals and care-consumers, the exhibition highlights the transformative potential of participatory design research in shaping more responsive, inclusive, and human-centred healthcare.
contributors: Adelaide University researchers; designers; healthcare professionals; care-consumers

title: YOKE, OBJECTS FOR HUMANS
blurb: YOKE • objects for human connection • explores the quiet power of handmade objects to draw us back toward one another in a time increasingly shaped by speed, convenience, and digital distance. Ceramics, furniture, vessels, lighting, plants and sculptural works become conduits for human closeness through thoughtful making, shared presence and storytelling.
contributors: Samantha Agostino; Simon Bajada; Andrew Carvolth; Thomas Carvolth; Miles Dunne; Em Frank; Daniel Guest; Ha Architecture; Alexandra Hirst; Denise Hojdyssek; Takeshi Iue; Joslin Koolen; Alexis Mason; Bridget Saville; Lea Tarakdjian; Eden Wellings

title: GROUNDED
blurb: Grounded is an exhibition at Fabrikate studio for Adelaide Design Week, partnering with Melbourne's Lander Se Gallery, curated by Hannah Nowlan. Ceramics, textile, art, sculpture and scent respond to one another in one immersive environment — design as connection, not collection, grounded in the hands and making that shaped it all.

title: ADW OPENING PARTY x SHORT NOTICE
WASTE RECONSIDERED
blurb: ‘WASTE RECONSIDERED’ an exploration of beauty within the discarded. Flipping the concept of landfill waste to produce elegant usable forms, Rebecca and Rachel work with local businesses and industries to source abundant waste streams and the result.. ASTONISHING.. an aesthetic story within our homes, workplaces and dining experiences.
contributors: Esse Bio Designs (Brand); Something Special Concept Store (host); Rebecca Hartman Kearns (Maker; Founder); Rachel Mifsud (Designer; Founder)

title: X KEULEMANS
blurb: Presented in partnership with Adelaide University, this exhibition showcases creative works by South Australian designer, artist and researcher Guy Keulemans. In collaboration with leading Australian designers, Keulemans explores the repair, reuse and generative and regenerative processes for environmental sustainability.

title: POWER SURGE: INTO THE GRID
blurb: An exhibition of prototype lighting by Associates of JamFactory’s Ceramics, Furniture, Glass and Jewellery/Metal Studios, providing insight into the creative process of design and production.

title: TOMORROW TALENT
blurb: Discover the next generation of designer/makers in an exhibition of work by the talented Associates across JamFactory’s Ceramics, Glass, Furniture and Jewellery/Metal Studios.

title: TOKEN
blurb: TOKEN / curated vending machine Travelling micro gallery & marketplace lucky dip celebrating the creativity, generosity and curiosity of our design community. Affordable, accessible and unexpected, TOKEN allows every*one to take home a small piece of Adelaide Design Week with all proceeds donated to Carlew.

title: PUBLIC NOTICE
blurb: Public Notice is an open poster exhibition presented as part of Adelaide Design Week, inviting graphic designers, students and visual communicators to use the poster as it was always meant to be used—as a tool for communication, not commerce. The exhibition takes its cues from the AGDA Poster Annuals: a theme, a format, and an open call. But there is no jury here and no selection process. The theme—design is not neutral. Every decision carries a point of view. Public Notice asks designers to respond to whatever that means to you: a social issue, an environmental concern, a community, a belief. The only brief is to stand for something.

title: CARDENING CLUB
blurb: Cardening Club playfully juxtaposes Mother Nature with human design. A roving planted vehicle moves through the city during Adelaide Design Week, creating unexpected moments of greenery. Appearing at key events and locations, the installation transforms an object designed for movement into a playful exploration of nature, creativity and urban design.

title: LIVING ON THE CEILING
blurb: Living on the ceiling is a lighting family resulting from exploring the relationship between material, memory and transformation. Through the use of ceramics and linen the show exhibits pieces made by imprinting, folding, creasing, bending and tearing porcelain with remnants of French workwear.

title: TORPOR DAY BED
blurb: Torpor seat is an object that investigates the relationship between rest, movement, and material reuse. The project brings together recycled denim textiles developed by Will Cheesman in collaboration with Nudie Jeans, with reclaimed timber sourced and crafted by Oliver Hyde.

title: ESTILO X MILLER KNOLL: AERON NEVER STOPS
DESIGNING YITPI
venue: Allan Scott, ADL Uni, ADL CBD

title: MADE HERE
blurb: Presented by Stylecraft, Made Here celebrates new local furniture design through an open studio showcase. Guest designer Helen Kontouris joins us in conversation about practice, craft, and the wider Australian design industry.

title: JAM FACTORY X GUY KEULEMANS
blurb: South Australian designer, artist and researcher Guy Keulemans provides insight into his current JamFactory exhibition 'X Guy Keulemans'

title: YOU'RE NOT FINISHED YET
venue: The Forum, Jeffrey Smart, ADL CBD
blurb: This panel is a provocation around craft, design, and professional practice, and how these connect to educating the next generations of practitioners. It positions craft as a critical and shared practice: a generative way of thinking and an ongoing discipline that begins with making and happens with others.
contributors: Lee-Anne Hall; Veronika Kelly; Guy Keulemans; Gabriella Bisetto

title: TORRENS RIVER CITY WALK
blurb: Walk the River Torrens like never before. Using an interactive mobile map, this guided walk reveals 150 years of urban design evolution. View archival photos of exact locations and see how GeoAI analyzed Adelaide's heritage landscape to track changes in infrastructure, vegetation, and public life.

title: WAX CARVING: RING MAKING
venue: Min Jewellery, G14 33 Pirie St, ADL
blurb: Wax carving ring making work shop. Work with wax and tools to design and shape your unique ring. Your wax design will be professionally cast, sanded, and finished by the instructor. In approximately two weeks, your completed sterling silver ring will be ready for you to collect

title: SUPER PARTY
blurb: A super late, super party. In 2020, Bankston Architectural and Sans-Arc launched the Super Collection into lockdown. No party, no fanfare. Five years and four collaborations later we're finally throwing it, inside Sans-Arc's new West Croydon studio. The collection draws on the Radical Design Movement, so does the night. Part exhibition, part installation, part party. Hospitality presented with a Bankston + Sans-Arc touch. Touch points throughout, an experience in one way or another. Drinks, food, music, fun.

title: ANTHO
blurb: Hygge Studio and Lo & Co Interiors present ANTHO, a study of botanics in motion through mechanical intervention. ANTHO explores the relationship between nature, technology, light, and atmosphere within interior space. Through kinetic movement and shadow play, the works reinterpret wind, blooming, and organic rhythm as sculptural, programmed experiences.

title: BLOOM
blurb: BLOOM is a collaborative exhibition showcasing multidisciplinary creatives, examining the individual and collective experience of the algal bloom that has affected our South Australian coastlines. Hosted at Basement Gallery, BLOOM platforms critical dialogue and fervour surrounding an ongoing ecological issue, explored through experimental visual art and design modes.
contributors: Ruby Yates (Co-Curator); Natasha Katsikas (Co-Curator); Poppy Chung; Nikita Mettananda; Rodrigo Kimblet; Oliver Johnson; Bianca Hoffrichter; Michael Waters; Phoebe Hunter; Chloe Burton; Kate Hendry; Francesca Narni; Chelsea Evans

title: SHOP GENERATOR
blurb: A temporary shop for permanent objects. Shop Generator brings together a curated collection of considered objects by independent designers and makers. Bridging the space between exhibition and retail, Shop Generator brings objects into focus to be encountered, celebrated and collected. Here for a moment, then gone again.

title: SOFT X AGSA
blurb: Through artworks, objects and encounters, Soft seeks to invite new connections and ways of seeing, while considering the quiet gestures of care and meaning that shape our relationship with the things we live alongside.
contributors: Sebastian Nocelli; Janice Cui; Jesse Wakenshaw; Belinda Nimmo; Phillip Nielsen; Em Franklin + Miles Dunne; Marlo Lyda; Studio Tops; Indigo Tolhurst; Patrick Scott; Dean Toepfer; Riley Stone; Tom Golin; Drew Abrahamson; Lotte Schwerdtfeger; Tom Graham; Penny Fisher; Julian Leigh May; AMALGAME studio; Tom Summers; Jay Jermyn

title: STARRY STARRY NIGHT
blurb: We’re going off grid. Taking a breath to explore the romance, ritual, deliberate nature of lighting the humble candle. Whether it’s amidst a stormy blackout, the final touch on the dinner party you’ve slaved for or to help you unwind after another busy day, there is no doubting the charm of candlelight. (Plus, everyone looks better candlelit). Starry starry night is a multidisciplinary exhibition showcasing contemporary craft and design. Exploring soft deliberate lighting and the way it can shape individual and shared sensory experience.

title: TWO WAY
blurb: Two-way is a collaborative exhibition, by a designer, jeweller, musician and a furniture maker, exploring the exchange between maker and material. The artworks are a result of attention, negotiation and participation rather than control. Two-way invites audiences to observe the conversations that occur through creative practice and our relationship with the material world.
contributors: Isabelle Byrne; Peter Fong; Emma Byrne; Will Young

title: BESPOKE INTENTION
blurb: Arc Tile Design invites you to discover limitless approaches and applications in Architecture and Design. Join renowned Interior Architect Susanna Bilardo from Enoki Design and Architect Sally Wilson from Archaea Architects. Unveiling a bespoke case study showcasing materiality longevity and shaping the future of the space, presented by Arc Tile Design.
contributors: Interior Architect Susanna Bilardo from Enoki Design; Architect Sally Wilson from Archaea Architects; Daniella Antonuccio Designer of Arc Tile Design

title: COVERS AND PAGES
blurb: Presented by Splinter Journal and Pink Shorts Press, as part of Adelaide Design Week 2026. Featuring Tamika Couedor (FutureJuice), Tyrone Ormsby (Person Books, designer of Splinter Journal) and Jess Zeng (ban she, zine maker), in conversation with Emily Hart (Pink Shorts Press). Free to attend. Come along for a glass of wine, an Imprints browse and to discuss everyone's opinions on book covers. Please get in touch with any questions or access requirements.
contributors: Tamika Couedor (FutureJuice); Tyrone Ormsby (Person Books; designer of Splinter Journal); Jess Zeng (ban she; zine maker); in conversation with Emily Hart (Pink Shorts Press)

title: DESIGNING DEEPLY
blurb: A thought-provoking panel discussion exploring the tension between universal design and designing for specific user needs. The session examines whether creating solutions for everyone can inadvertently dilute effectiveness, and how deeply addressing niche requirements can generate broader societal benefits. When everyone is different, how do we design for anyone?
contributors: Dr Nathan James Crane; Eric Cross – Circ Industrial Design; Kiri Bowmer – JPE Design Studio; Keith Dougal – JPE Design Studio (Facilitator)

title: DESIGNING FUTURES
venue: The Forum, Jeffrey Smart, ADL CBD

title: IN CONVERSATION
blurb: Join Rebecca Evans, Curator of Decorative Arts and Design for a special Adelaide Design Week Tuesday Talk with South Australian craftsperson and designer, Jon Goulder. Jon Goulder is a fourth-generation furniture designer and maker. Goulder completed his apprenticeship in furniture making and upholstery with his family’s business E W Goulder and Sons, between 1988-1992. In 1996 he moved to Canberra to study furniture design and fine woodworking at Canberra School of Art under the direction of the late George Ingham. After leaving Canberra School of Art he established his design consultancy – ’Jon Goulder Designer Maker’. Goulder is both a designer and a talented furniture maker- a rarity in the Australian and international design community. Between 2013-2018 he was Creative Director (Furniture) Jam Factory Adelaide, he was previously a Senior Designer with Snohetta Architects Australasia. He currently runs his own studio space in the southern suburbs of Adelaide.

title: MONET TO MATISSE : ART TO EXHIBITION
blurb: Go behind the scenes of Monet to Matisse: Defying Tradition with AGSA's curatorial team and exhibition designers Grieve Gillett Architects. Discover how art, architecture, colour and curatorial thinking came together to shape the exhibition, from the placement of individual works to the design of the complete visitor experience.
contributors: GGA exhibition design team + AGSA curatorial team

title: THE DIGITAL PAUSE - COLLAGE EVENING
venue: Being Studio, 27 Halifax St, ADL CBD
blurb: Together with Klaro, we’re hosting an analogue collage night, The Digital Pause! Join us for a relaxed evening to unplug, unwind, and create your own vision board for the design practice you want to manifest. We’ll have magazines, fabric offcuts and catalogues on hand, plus some refreshments.

title: 10 X 10
blurb: 10x10 Same Parameters, Different Outcomes

title: A ROOM OF ONE'S OWN
blurb: A Room of One's Own is a collaborative examination of interior living through applied arts. Inspired by the interdisciplinary approach of the Bloomsbury Group and research into the Powerhouse Museum’s collection, the artists work across sculpture, furniture and functional objects, blurring the line between art, design and the decorative.
contributors: Eleanor Amor; Agatha Gothe-Snape; Jennifer Mathews; Michelle Nikou; Nat Penney

title: AFTERLIFE
blurb: Afterlife is a research project investigating the reuse of demolished concrete. The exhibition seeks to change how permanence and decay are read in architecture, urging a more conscious consumption of a material that has potential beyond waste.

title: AT THE TABLE
blurb: At the Table is an immersive dining experience, bringing together food, design, and community through the most universal of rituals - sharing a meal. Presented as a ticketed sit-down dinner hosted by Bar Pin, the event invites twenty-two guests per sitting to engage with locally made design.

title: BENCHED
blurb: True

title: NOW: NEW/OLD WORKS
blurb: NOW: new/old work brings together creations and archival pieces from artists in residence and alumni of Washdog Studios and fab workshop. Celebrating creative evolution, this exhibition maps the bridge between past explorations and current practices revealing how early ideas transform, persist and re-emerge in contemporary design and art.

title: SKANGAROOVIA
blurb: Skangaroovia is a South Australian design studio specialising in lighting, furniture and crafted objects. We collaborate with architects and designers to create project-specific outcomes that are thoughtful, practical and finely crafted. This exhibition introduces our practice through past and current projects. It highlights our in-house design and making capabilities.
contributors: Mark Jones; Ellis Moseley; Yuro Cuchor; Marlize DeKlerk; Lex Stobie

title: STEEL SKIN (performance)
blurb: STEEL SKIN is an immersive Adelaide Design Week performance where artists Pierre Mukeba, James Geue (Discarded), Alix Kuijpers, Liam Somerville and more combine interactive sound, movement and visuals. Audiences are invited to interact, shaping an evolving sensory experience that blurs the boundaries between installation, live performance, participation and contemporary design.
contributors: Alix Kuijpers; Izabella Vozzo; Jack Green; James Geue; Liam Somerville; Pierre Mukeba

title: UNBUILT
blurb: Unbuilt explores the tension between absence and presence within projects that were never built. Through immersive installations, projections, drawings, and models, audiences are invited into imagined environments that almost existed. Curated by EmAGN for Adelaide Design Week, the exhibition celebrates experimentation, ambition, and creative practice across disciplines.
contributors: EmAGN; PARABOLICA (others TBC including Moraene; Craft Architecture; Studio Philo; potentially lighting design by House of Vnholy)

title: YES YOU CAN DO A PHD
venue: The Forum, Jeffrey Smart, ADL CBD
blurb: To be provided shortly
contributors: Melinda Gaughwin; Nathan James Crane; Bec Boland; Eric Luksch; Anna Goldsmith

title: INSIDE INNOVATION: INSIDE QANTAS TOUR
blurb: Interior designers are invited to join us for a walk-through of Qantas’ newly opened Product Innovation Centre in Adelaide. The tour will be led by Concept CI, the interior designer behind the space, together with Klaro Industrial Design, who supplied the furniture. Together, they’ll take guests through key elements of the interior, design decisions and furniture solutions in an informal, conversational format.
contributors: Concept CI; Klaro Industrial Design; Qantas

title: ADW CLOSING PARTY X COMPANY WORKS
MADE IN AUS
blurb: 4FE present a thoughtful curation of objects sourced exclusively from private collection showcasing the influence of migrant and local talents in furniture art, industrial design, and manufacturing in Australia between the 1950s-1980s. These iconic pieces are displayed through a fresh contemporary lens, exemplifying how good design transcends time.
contributors: Grant; Mary Featherston; Douglas Snelling; Johan H Naess; Fred Lowen; More

title: MAKING SPACE
blurb: Months of planning. Years of emotion. A lifespan of less than a day. Making space for the temporary environments of floristry in the world of installation design.
contributors: Collating a finalised list - more people coming on board

title: NEO TEEN TAKEOVER: LET'S GOGH
blurb: Celebrate Monet to Matisse with a full gallery takeover. Check out live music, artist workshops and new projects from the state's leading youth and arts organisations.
contributors: Mixed Goods Studio (ADW); 10 Youth orgs TBC; Artists for event: Billie Justice Thompson; Arlon Hall

title: TO FEEL IN PLACE
blurb: Here the many pieces have a place. Here we find the comfort we crave. We inhibit many spaces, engage in many environments and interact with many people. But what does it mean to feel truly ‘In Place’? Join photographer and designer, Studio Philo in a photographical and written exploration of our environments and what it means to truly ‘belong’. Made possible by Atkins Lab and EmAGN SA.
contributors: Studio Philo In Collaboration with Atkins Lab

title: UNDER A BRIDGE
blurb: Jake Rollins presents Under a Bridge, a two-hour pop-up exhibition of new works specific to site. Adelaide location, bridge announced on the day.

title: MIXED GOODS: OPEN STUDIO
blurb: Join us at Mixed Goods Studios for a special Adelaide Design Week Open Studio. Wander through the studios, meet the designers, artists and makers behind the work, and gain an insight into their creative processes. Explore works in progress, finished pieces and material experiments by Andrew Carvolth, Dean Toepfer, Danielle Barrie, Sam Gold, Bridget Saville, Carman Skeehan, Joslin Koolen and Thomas Carvolth.
contributors: Andrew Carvolth; Dean Toepfer; Danielle Barrie; Sam Gold; Bridget Saville; Carman Skeehan; Joslin Koolen; Thomas Carvolth

title: YADURA: OPEN HOUSE
blurb: Yadura is our home and studio in South Australia, a warm, creative space filled with art, sculpture, and stories from Adelaide, the Middle East, and the places we have lived and traveled. More than a studio, it is a house of light, life, and storytelling, where creativity is part of everyday living. This event opens Yadura to friends and community, inviting you to experience a space that carries memory, culture, and imagination.

title: METIS (Navigating Systems Change)
blurb: The systems we inherited are breaking. A crisis? or an Opening? > > > METIS a talk//reflection on systems change: what's collapsing, what’s emerging at the margins, and how to locate your role inside inside the shift. We’re designing a new world. Feel the pull? Let’s navigate together.

title: THE FRINGE CONDITION: EXTREME DESIGN
blurb: What does it mean to design for life at the fringe of human existence? The Fringe Condition is an exhibition and panel discussion exploring one of the most radical design briefs of our time, building for human life on the Moon, and what that means for communities here on Earth.
contributors: Amit Srivastava; Albert Rajkumar; Meriem Allani; Souktik Bhattacherjee; Monika Stankiewicz; Kato Claeys; Kara Simpson

title: EVERY*BIKE TOUR
blurb: The Every*bike Tour is a casual cycling tour connecting ADW exhibitions, events, designers, studios, curators, makers, workshops, artists, galleries, places and people together by bike. Each stop along the way is a chance to meet, learn and discover an exciting and energised creative Adelaide! BYO Bike :)

title: LISTENING WITH ARCHITECTURE
venue: Jewels of Thought Records, ADL CBD
blurb: What kinds of acoustic spaces does the architecture of our city offer us? How might these spaces ground us. How might they serve to expand our sense of self? Join artist and educator Tom Borgas on a guided listening experience of some of his favourite east-end pockets of sonic intensity.

title: THREADING STORIES
blurb: Threading Stories is a community quilting workshop grounded in care, creativity and storytelling. This workshop allows participants to sew or embellish a shared quilt. Open to everyone from beginner to advanced sewers and storytellers, to printmakers, painters and mixed media creatives.

title: AFTER HOURS
blurb: After Hours celebrates emerging female creatives and the work made beyond the boundaries of their everyday professions. Bringing together diverse creative disciplines, the exhibition transforms a shared space into a studio, archive and gathering place - revealing the ideas, experiments and personal practices that emerge after hours.
contributors: Elaine Thomas; Maddy Cabalao; Kiri Bowmer; Tamara Montina; Ava Kim; Alisa Vakhtangova; Kathryn Neale; Chloe Katopodis; Zoe Grigoris; Gigi O'Halloran; Kate Maiden; Anny Benjamin; Mengzhu Jiang; Leia Ahmed; Ziyan Qi; Rita Liao; Bridget Saville; Whitney Huang; Minqi Gu; Min Jeong; Lena Rowe

title: TAC COLLECTION
blurb: "taC" seating is a collaboration between brothers Andrew and Thomas Carvolth. Made locally in their studio, each piece is direct in form and generous in feel.

title: ÉMIGRÉ: SPEAKER SERIES
blurb: Émigré brings together art, design and architecture for one afternoon at Lynton Residence, a 1962 mid-century home by émigré architect Hubert van der Pennen. Two curated sessions ask who shapes a city, and from where: first through overlooked urban space, then through the practitioners who arrived from elsewhere.
contributors: Stuart Symons; Jet O'Rourke; Chloe Tanner; Richard Le Messurier; Tom Borgas; Julia Townsend; more

title: MODERNIST ADELAIDE WALKING TOUR
blurb: Adelaide's mid-century boom produced a revolution of modernist architecture most locals walk past without a glance. Stuart Symons' award-winning tours have drawn international acclaim and a devoted cult following, tracing how global design ideas took flight in Adelaide during the 1950s–70s. 'Jewel-like' – Kevin McCloud, Grand Designs
